title: A Life of Buddha (Buddhacarita)
author: asvaghosha
attributionNote: The Buddhacarita is ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa, the poet and dramatist of the early Kuṣāṇa period. The Sanskrit original survives only for the first half; this translation is Beal's English rendering of the Chinese version made by Dharmarakṣa in 420 CE, which preserves all twenty-eight chapters.
description: Aśvaghoṣa's Life of the Buddha is the great Buddhist epic: the birth at Lumbinī, the palace years and the four sights, the departure from the city, the years of austerity, the defeat of Māra and the enlightenment, the first sermon, the conversion of the disciples and the Buddha's final extinction. Written in the polished Sanskrit of the kāvya court poets, it turns the Buddha's biography into a meditation on impermanence and kingship, and its Chinese version made it one of the most influential narratives in East Asian Buddhism.
historicalContext: Aśvaghoṣa wrote at the court of Kaniṣka in the 2nd century CE, and the Buddhacarita is the earliest complete Buddhist biography in classical Sanskrit. Dharmarakṣa's Chinese translation of 420 CE, the Fo-Sho-Hing-Tsan-King, was rendered into English by Samuel Beal for the Sacred Books of the East in 1883; Beal's version, with its notes on the Sanskrit and Chinese readings, is the text streamed here.
availabilityNote: Complete. All twenty-eight vargas of Beal's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one varga per chapter. The volume's title page, contents, introduction and index are not part of the work; the translator's notes on each page are kept.
